sections.h2: Selling fast in Round Lake Beach
sections.html:
You can list on the market, sell privately, or sell directly to a buyer paying cash. The direct sale is quickest, but every route runs through the village's occupancy permit, which is required before a residential property is sold. Start that permit at least two weeks before closing so the date does not slip.

  • Listing the house brings the most exposure, along with showings and repair requests.
  • Selling it yourself saves the commission and puts the paperwork on you.
  • A direct sale to a cash buyer is usually as-is and closes when you are ready.

Round Lake Beach is a northern Lake County village with an estimated 26,902 residents, down 1.3% from 2020. It has 8,537 households averaging 3.16 people, and 79.3% of units are owner-occupied. The middle home value is $199,200 and the middle gross rent is $1,543.

Family-sized houses are the norm. At this price level, a new roof or furnace weighs heavily against what a house sells for, so repair bills push many owners toward as-is offers. Commuters like the village's Metra North Central Service station, with weekday trains to Chicago Union Station, and the road links along Rollins Road and Cedar Lake Road. Round Lake Area School District 116 serves the village, and the district can confirm the boundary for a single address.

Round Lake Beach requires every residential property to obtain an Occupancy Permit before it is sold. The permit moves water and sewer service from seller to buyer and confirms the exterior is maintained and up to code. Contact the village at least two weeks before closing.

  • Fill out the online occupancy application, select the address and choose the Occupancy permit type.
  • Attach photos of the water meter.
  • After the application is accepted, pay the $60 fee through the emailed link.
  • The inspection is scheduled after payment. It covers the exterior only, and no one has to be present.
  • Five days before closing, email a photo of the inside meter reading and the outside receiver reading, if there is one, so the final water bill can be calculated.

The final water bill must be paid before the buyers can pick up the occupancy certificate. Call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 as soon as you set the closing date.

Water and sewer bills go out every two months, in January, March, May, July, September and November. A bill left unpaid after its due date can carry a 10% late fee. New owners pay a deposit billed on their first bill, refundable only after ownership or tenancy changes and the final bill is paid in full.

Charges run per 1,000 gallons, plus per-bill customer and sewer fees and a phosphorus surcharge for regional treatment at the Fox Lake facility. Rates change, so ask Village Hall for the current schedule before you estimate your final bill.

sections.h2: If the house is a rental
sections.html:
Rental owners follow a separate annual certification program. Landlords get a notice in early to mid October with inspection times, deadlines and fees. Requirements include a submitted application, the certification fee, a passed inspection with deficiencies resolved, current Crime Free certification, and no outstanding liens or payments owed to the village.

Miss the deadline and you pay a $100 late fee and get a two-week extension. After that the property can go to adjudication with an additional $1,500 fine and liens. Landlords new to the village must attend a Crime-Free Housing seminar or show proof of certification from another Chicagoland municipality. Call 847-546-2351 for seminar information. If tenants live in the house, confirm the certification is current before you accept a contract, because a buyer's title company may ask about liens.

sections.h2: Transfer taxes and who records the deed
sections.html:
The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division collects state and county transfer taxes at recording: 50 cents per $500 for the state and 25 cents per $500 for the county, issued as a single stamp. The county's pamphlet says either buyer or seller may pay, so check your contract. A state transfer declaration (PTAX-203) goes with the deed unless an exemption statement is signed.

The Recording Division is at 18 N County St, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. Some communities require their own transfer stamp, among them Buffalo Grove, Highland Park, Lake Forest, Lincolnshire, Mettawa and North Chicago. Round Lake Beach is not on that county list, but confirm with Village Hall.

Lake County mails tax bills on May 1, with the first installment due in June and the second in September. The county posts each year's calendar on its Treasurer pages. Ask your title company to prorate the bill on the closing statement, and check whether both installments are paid before you set a date.

sections.h2: Round Lake Beach timeline for a quick closing
sections.html: A fast sale here comes down to a few appointments. Once a buyer is lined up, apply for the occupancy permit and pay the fee. Wait for the exterior inspection, which needs no one at home. Five days before closing, email the meter photos, then pay the final water bill so the buyers can collect the certificate. A cash buyer has no lender appraisal to wait for, so these steps usually set the pace. Keep the water account current while the house is empty, because an open balance holds up the certificate.

faqs.q: Do I need an occupancy permit to sell in Round Lake Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. Residential properties must obtain an Occupancy Permit before sale. The fee is $60 and the inspection covers the exterior only.

faqs.q: How early should I start the permit?
faqs.a: At least two weeks before closing. The final water reading also goes in about five days ahead, so call the Finance Department at 847-546-2351 once the date is set.

faqs.q: Does anyone need to be home for the inspection?
faqs.a: No. The occupancy inspection is exterior only, and no one is required to be present.

faqs.q: What is the water deposit for new owners?
faqs.a: A $100 deposit billed on the buyer's first water and sewer bill. It is refundable only after the property changes ownership or tenancy and the final bill is paid in full.

faqs.q: Which office records a Round Lake Beach deed?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. It collects the state and county stamps and records the stamped deed.
